summary.text: A 30-year-old Chinese woman presented with fatigue, yellowish discoloration of the eyes and dark urine for 4 months. She had been a heavy drinker, was diagnosed with hemolytic anemia at a first local hospitalization and prescribed oral prednisolone for 2 months, after which her symptoms worsened. A second hospitalization one month before admission to this hospital diagnosed severe acute pancreatitis with triglycerides of 311.87 mg/dL.

At this hospital she had scleral icterus, facial and conjunctival edema, moon face, central obesity, a palpable liver and spleen and mild lower-limb edema. Smear, bone marrow, ultrasound, CT and liver biopsy findings were recorded, and thalassaemia, hereditary spherocytosis and viral, autoimmune and metabolic liver disease were ruled out.

The diagnosis was Zieve syndrome based on cholestasis, hemolytic anemia and alcoholic liver disease. Treatment consisted of alcohol abstinence, blood transfusion, glutathione, diuretics, ursodeoxycholic acid, vitamins and cefoperazone sodium/tazobactam sodium, and her condition gradually improved.

She was discharged with orders to withdraw completely from alcohol and take glutathione, ursodeoxycholic acid and polysaccharide iron complex. The abstract and case text disagree on the interval to discharge (14 versus 25 days). Two months after discharge liver size, portal vein diameter, glucose, hemoglobin, bilirubin, ALP and gamma-glutamyltransferase were almost normalized and her general condition was well.
